newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn closes lower on weather forecasts, funds.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn closes lower on weather forecasts, funds.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed lower on forecasts for better harvest next week, fund selling and on commercial selling tied to hedge sales, traders said.
Action in the options pit also contributed pressure, they said.

Rosenthal Collins bought 2,000 December $3.00 puts at 5-1/2 to 6-1/4 cents and sold 1,000 December $3.10 puts at 10-1/2 to 10-3/4 cents, options traders said. E.D. and F. Man International sold 2,000 December $2.90 puts at 2-1/2 to three cents, the traders said.

Midwest weather was a mixed bag. While the outlooks for drier weather next week weighed on the market, the wet, cool weather this week was slowing corn harvest in the United States and keeping cash basis markets firm.
In the futures pit, Continental Grain sold two million bushels of December, R.J. O'Brien and Rosenthal Collins each sold one million December, they said.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 48,000, down from 77,133 Thursday, according to the CBOT.
Corn futures closed 1/2 to 2-3/4 cents a bushel lower, with December down 2-3/4 at $3.03-1/4. March closed two cents per bushel lower at $3.10-1/2.
Options volume was estimated at 22,000, down from 34,356 Thursday.
